subject: Physics
question_text: What do you think did Einstein mean when he said: “The most incomprehensible thing about the world is that it is comprehensible”?
answer_text: The Physical world around us is full of different complex natural phenomena so the world is in-comprehensible. But with the help of study and observations it has been found that all these phenomena are based on some basic physical laws and so it is comprehensible.
final_answer: Thus, the world is comprehensible through the understanding of basic physical laws.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of Einstein's perspective on science and nature.

subject: Physics
question_text: Give some examples from the history of science of the validity of the remark: “Every great physical theory starts as a heresy and ends as a dogma”.
answer_text: The statement above is true. Validity of this incisive remark can be validated from the example of moment of inertia. It states that the moment of inertia of a body depends on its energy. But according to Einstein's mass-energy relation (E = mc²), energy depends on the speed of the body.
final_answer: Therefore, the moment of inertia example illustrates the transition from heresy to dogma in scientific theories.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding historical context and examples in science.

subject: Physics
question_text: Explain the aphorism: “Politics is the art of the possible”. Similarly, “Science is the art of the soluble”.
answer_text: It is well known that to win over votes, politicians would make anything and everything possible even when they are least sure of the same. And in Science, the various natural phenomena can be explained in terms of some basic laws. So as 'Politics is the art of possible' similarly 'Science is the art of the soluble'.
final_answer: Thus, both politics and science deal with what can be achieved or explained.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of the analogy between politics and science.

subject: Physics
question_text: Name some important factors that have hindered the advancement of science in India.
answer_text: Some important factors which have hindered the advancement of science in India are: Proper funds are not arranged for the development of research work and laboratories. The labs and scientific instruments are very old and outdated. Most of the people in India are uneducated and highly traditional. They don't understand the importance of Science. There is no proper employment opportunity for the science educated person in India. There are no proper facilities for science education in schools and colleges in India.
final_answer: These factors collectively hinder the growth of scientific advancement in India.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves analysis of socio-economic factors affecting science.

subject: Physics
question_text: How will you refute the argument that ‘ghosts’ exist even though no one has '‘seen'’ one?
answer_text: No physicist has ever seen an atom but there are practical evidences which prove the presence of electron. Their size is so small, even powerful microscopes find it difficult to measure their sizes. But still its effects could be tested. On the other end, there is no phenomena which can be explained on the basis of existence of ghosts. Our senses of sight and hearing are very limited to observe the existence of both. So there is no comparison between the two given cases.
final_answer: Therefore, the existence of electrons is supported by evidence, unlike ghosts.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires critical thinking and understanding of scientific evidence.

subject: Physics
question_text: Which of the two explanations regarding the crab shells resembles a scientific explanation?
answer_text: The second explanation is scientific: After the sea tragedy, fishermen in that area, in a gesture of honor to their dead hero, let free any crab shell caught by them which accidentally had a shape resembling the face of a Samurai. Consequently, the particular shape of the crab shell survived longer and therefore in course of time the shape was genetically propagated. This is an example of evolution by artificial selection.
final_answer: Thus, the second explanation illustrates a scientific approach to understanding the phenomenon.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding of evolutionary concepts and artificial selection.

subject: Physics
question_text: What were the key scientific and technological advances that triggered the industrial revolution in England and Western Europe more than two centuries ago?
answer_text: More than two centuries ago, England and Western Europe invented steam engine, electricity, theory of gravitation and the explosives. Steam engines helped them in the field of heat and thermodynamics, theory of gravitation in field of motion and making guns and cannons. These progresses brought about industrial revolution in England and Western Europe.
final_answer: Thus, the key advances included the steam engine, electricity, theory of gravitation, and explosives.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of historical context and basic application of knowledge.

subject: Physics
question_text: List some key contemporary areas of science and technology, which are responsible for the second industrial revolution.
answer_text: Some of the key contemporary areas of science and technology which may transform the society radically are: Development of super fast computers, Internet and tremendous advancement in information technology, Development in Biotechnology, Development of super-conducting materials at room temperature, Development of robots.
final_answer: These areas include super fast computers, the Internet, biotechnology, superconducting materials, and robotics.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires knowledge of current technological advancements and their implications.

subject: Physics
question_text: Formulate your views on the practice of science when a discovery has great academic interest but dangerous consequences for society.
answer_text: In our view, a type of discovery which is of great academic interest but harmful for human society should not be made public because Science is for the society, society is not for science.
final_answer: Therefore, harmful discoveries should be kept confidential to protect society.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves ethical reasoning and personal reflection on the implications of scientific discoveries.

subject: Physics
question_text: How will you use your knowledge of science to develop strategies to counter superstitious and obscurantist attitudes in society?
answer_text: Poverty and illiteracy are the two major factors which make people superstitious in India. So to remove the superstitious and obscurantist attitude we have to first overcome these factors. Everybody should be educated, so that one can have scientific attitude. Knowledge of science can be put to use to prove people's superstitious wrong by showing them the scientific logic behind everything happening in our world.
final_answer: Thus, education and scientific reasoning can help counter superstitious beliefs.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires understanding of social issues and application of scientific knowledge.

subject: Physics
question_text: Demolish the view that women do not have the innate nature, capacity and intelligence, using scientific arguments and examples of great women.
answer_text: To demolish this view there are many examples of women who have proven their abilities in Science and other fields. Madam Curie, Mother Teresa, Indira Gandhi, Marget Thatcher, Rani Laxmi Bai, Florence Nightingale are some examples. So in this era women are definitely not behind man in any field.
final_answer: Therefore, women have proven their capabilities in various fields, demonstrating equality with men.
difficulty_reasoning: Involves understanding gender equality and citing examples.

subject: Physics
question_text: Criticize the statement: 'It is more important to have beauty in the equations of physics than to have them agree with experiments'.
answer_text: An equation which agrees with experiment must also be simple and hence beautiful. We have some simple and beautiful equations in Physics such as E = mc², E = hv, KE = 1/2mv², PE = mgh, W = F.d. All have the same dimensions. One experiment shows dependency of energy on speed, the other shows dependency on frequency & displacement. That's the beauty of equations in Physics coming from different experiments.
final_answer: Thus, beauty in equations is often linked to their simplicity and experimental validation.
difficulty_reasoning: Requires critical thinking and understanding of the relationship between theory and experiment.
